Explanation:  
The Predicted Answer accurately states that when Miller Williams began his graduate studies (around 1951–52), the schools in his hometown of Hoxie, Arkansas, were still racially segregated. It further elaborates that desegregation did not occur until 1955, after the Brown v. Board of Education decision—matching the Ground Truth Answer, which says, "They were segregated until 1955. Miller Williams began working on his master's in 1952." The substantive information—that the schools were still segregated when Williams began his master’s in 1952, and that they remained so until 1955—is clearly present in the Predicted Answer.

Decision: TRUE
